title: Global social progress is approaching a turning point as rights decline and gains in health, housing, information, and environmental quality stall or reverse
source_unit: Social Progress Imperative, 2026 Global Social Progress Index
geography: 171 countries covering more than 99% of the world’s population, with country and regional comparisons from 2011-2025

observations.period: 2011-2025; Global Social Progress Index coverage and framework

denominator.unit: countries covering more than 99% of the world’s population

indicator_set.unit: social and environmental progress drivers measured by the 2026 index

dimensions.value: Basic Needs, Foundations of Wellbeing, and Opportunity

economic_boundary.value: the index focuses on non-economic social performance rather than treating GDP as the outcome itself

time_series.value: the index provides a 15-year comparison spanning 2011-2025

observations.method: Composite Social Progress Index using 57 social and environmental outcome indicators across Basic Needs, Foundations of Wellbeing, and Opportunity, with country and regional comparisons over time.
observations.uncertainty: A composite index depends on indicator selection, weighting, imputation, comparability, and data quality; it is not a causal model of social progress or a direct measure of lived experience.
observations.subgroup: Countries and regions, populations exposed to different rights, health, safety, housing, information, environmental, and opportunity conditions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Index movement can reveal broad areas for attention without implying that every component moves together or that national performance is uniform within countries.

observations.period: 2011-2025; global rights, health, safety, environment, housing, and information trends

denominator.unit: countries in the Global Social Progress Index time series

rights_change.unit: nearly points decline in global rights since 2011

recent_rights_change.unit: points decline in rights from 2021 to 2025

recent_quality_change.value: health, safety, and environmental quality declined from 2021 to 2025

slowing_components.value: water and sanitation, housing, and access to information slowed significantly in the recent period

observations.method: Longitudinal comparison of index components and country-level social-progress scores from 2011 through 2025.
observations.uncertainty: Changes describe index performance and may reflect measurement, reporting, structural, political, environmental, and economic factors; the index does not identify one causal driver for each component.
observations.subgroup: Residents of countries with different rights, health, safety, environmental, housing, water, sanitation, and information conditions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Some countries and components continue to improve even within a global slowdown; deterioration is a portfolio-level warning, not a universal experience.

denominator.unit: countries in the 2026 Global Social Progress Index comparison

declined.unit: countries reported as declining in social progress

unchanged.unit: countries reported as showing no significant change

political_context.value: the Social Progress Imperative links a broad rights decline to rising authoritarian and populist leadership and warns of possible further deterioration

observations.method: Country-level comparison of recent index change, paired with Social Progress Imperative interpretation of rights and political leadership patterns.
observations.uncertainty: The leadership relationship is an interpretive association in the publisher’s analysis, not a causal estimate; country counts depend on significance thresholds and index construction.
observations.subgroup: Countries with different political systems, rights environments, public services, and social and environmental outcomes.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stagnation or decline can be reversed through institutional, social, environmental, and public-service improvements; the index identifies risk, not destiny.

observations.period: 2011-2025; social outcomes relative to economic resources

denominator.unit: country comparisons of social progress and GDP per capita

gdp_boundary.value: GDP per capita does not determine social progress; countries at similar income levels can have materially different social outcomes

denmark_us.value: Denmark and the United States have similar GDP per capita, while the United States scores nearly 10 points lower on social progress in the index

us_rank_change.unit: places the United States has slipped in the index ranking since 2011

us_component_decline.value: the United States declined in all 12 index components, with rights, housing, advanced education, inclusiveness, basic education, and safety each down more than 3 points

observations.method: Cross-sectional and longitudinal comparison of Social Progress Index scores with GDP per capita and component-level country performance.
observations.uncertainty: The GDP comparison is descriptive and does not establish which policies or institutions cause higher social progress; country-level averages can hide internal inequality.
observations.subgroup: Countries with similar or different economic resources, residents experiencing varying rights, housing, education, safety, and inclusion conditions, and policymakers using GDP as a progress proxy.
observations.counterinterpretation: Economic resources can enable social investment, but conversion into well-being depends on institutions, distribution, public choices, and social and environmental conditions.

related_sources.claim: Social Progress Index methodology and indicator framework.
Interactive country scorecards, time series, results deck, and data-access context.

boundary: This record adds a global social-progress route across rights, health, safety, environmental quality, water, sanitation, housing, information, education, inclusion, opportunity, and the limits of GDP as a progress measure. It uses a composite index and publisher interpretation, not a causal political-economy model, respondent-level lived-experience data, a complete within-country distributional account, or proof that rights decline causes every other component to worsen.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official Social Progress Imperative 2026 index page reviewed for the 171-country frame, 57 indicators, three dimensions, 2011-2025 time series, global rights and component changes, country-change counts, GDP comparison, and US ranking claims.
